As noone here seems to have read that you want to connect to an existing session:

x11vnc http://www.karlrunge.com/x11vnc/ From: http://serverfault.com/questions/27044/how-to-vnc-into-an-existing-x-session

VNC encryption is questionable at best, but can piggyback over ssh instead. So... just disable encryption with only listening to local. So an un-encrypted vnc server is insecure but not accessible. Then just have ssh connect to it.
"ssh user@vncserver.example.com -L 5901:127.0.0.1:5901 Xvnc -interface 127.0.0.1 'other vnc options' "

VNC on the client just connects to localhost:5901 which encrypts everything and send it across the net to the real server.

Install putty. It has an easy menu for linking remote and local ports together. Save as named connection and leave all the options set for next time. It's been a bit since I've used putty, but I remember it does a good job of saving the options after a working combination is found.

This guy's got it. If you want to get into an existing session, then VNC is really your best option, but its encryption is flaky as hell, as you've discovered. You're already going over a VPN, so your traffic is encrypted to an outside observer. You could add another layer of encryption by passing the traffic through an ssh tunnel, obfuscating it from anyone who might be sniffing your local network -- but to be honest, if you're worried about that, then you have bigger problems. If you just want to do this, and trust me I get that, then setting up an ssh tunnel for your VNC traffic across your existing VPN is going to be the easiest and most reliable method. There's a ton of material out there to show you how to do this using PuTTY.
